key_insight: Counterfactual bias in open-source LLMs for pediatric ED triage varies widely by model, and larger or medical-domain models are not automatically fairer.
clinical_relevance: For clinical decision support, this suggests model choice should include fairness auditing because demographic or context changes can shift acuity predictions even when the clinical vignette is unchanged.
method: Paired real and handbook-style pediatric ED vignettes with one counterfactual variable changed at a time.
Compared ten open-source LLMs, including base, instruction-tuned, fine-tuned, and medical-domain models.
Measured any shift, undertriage, overtriage, large shifts, mean shift, and mean absolute shift.
evidence_signal: Across ten models, the fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B had the lowest sensitivity (5.27% any-shift; mean absolute shift 0.0534), while the base model reached 16.02% and 0.1706.
watch_item: These results come from synthetic counterfactual vignettes, so real-world deployment should verify whether the same bias patterns hold in live clinical workflows.
paper_title: Counterfactual Auditing of Bias in Open-Source Large Language Models for Clinical Triage
